Algebra 2 · Unit 1: Equations and Inequalities

Solving Equations and Modeling Constraints

Turn real constraints into equations and inequalities, solve them, check every candidate, and decide what the answer means.

What you’ll learn

  • Translate a real situation into an equation or inequality
  • Solve compound inequalities and write them in interval notation
  • Solve a rational inequality using the sign of the variable
  • Check a solution by substituting it into the original equation
  • Decide what a solution means in context, and whether it makes sense
  • Apply domain restrictions to a model
  • Recognize when an equation has no real solution

Helps to know first: Multi-Step Equations (Algebra 1).

The mountain biking connection

Race prep runs on constraints: sag inside a 25–30% window, a stage time to beat, a climb you can only measure from the side. Each one is an equation or inequality to solve.

Learning activities

Interactive lab

Race-Day Workshop

Join an enduro team’s technical crew: check suspension sag with formulas and absolute value, work out the speed a stage needs with rational equations, and survey a climb with a radical equation, then pass the Race-Day Certification.

Level
Intermediate to Advanced
Time
20-25 min
  • 3 missions
  • Sag calculator and tolerance gauge
  • Race clock simulator
  • Trail survey simulator
  • Algebra debugger
  • Race-Day Certification (6)
  • Optional complex-number extension
